FOUR ITEMS ELIXIR-DEV FLAGGED FOR REVIEWER (each already independently checked by SECURITY-REVIEWER -- see the referenced report's items 1-4 for full detail; carried forward here since REVIEWER's own sign-off/judgement is separately required on items 1 and 4):

1. NEW DIRECT DEPENDENCY, REVIEWER SIGN-OFF REQUIRED: mix.exs now has {:telemetry, "~> 1.4"}. Confirmed a promotion, not a new fetch -- mix.lock diff is EMPTY (git diff main...HEAD -- mix.lock produces no output), mix.exs diff is +12/-0 (all comment plus the one line). SECURITY-REVIEWER has already granted its own sign-off (zero new attack surface -- telemetry is a pub/sub primitive with no I/O). REQ-194's own AC3 requires REVIEWER's sign-off be recorded in this PR too, regardless of the promotion's lighter risk profile -- please record it explicitly in your own result before this merges.

2. LABEL-ALLOWLIST INVARIANT (the entire safety mechanism for GET /metrics being global+unauthenticated): SECURITY-REVIEWER read every handle_task_completed/3, handle_event_append_stop/3, handle_repo_query/3, handle_http_request/3 function body in lib/letflow/metrics/registry.ex directly and confirmed none can ever extract a tenant_id/instance_id/definition_id/task_id/actor_id into a label -- family 2 (task_completions_total) is labelled definition_status (closed 4-value enum) only, never definition_id. lib/letflow/plugs/http_metrics.ex's route-template labeling was confirmed to only ever emit Plug.Router.match_path/1's compile-time template or the literal 'unmatched' constant. This is SECURITY-REVIEWER's domain and is now PASSED -- flagged here for your own awareness/idiom review of the same module, not as an open question.

3. conn.private[:plug_route] CORRECTION: ELIXIR-DEV corrected the design's claim that this key is unset on an unmatched request -- verified accurate by SECURITY-REVIEWER against the real deps/plug/lib/plug/router.ex source (extract_path/1 rewrites a bare match _ clause to the literal "/*_path" at compile time, line 663-664, so :plug_route is always set; Plug.Router.match_path/1's Map.fetch!/2 therefore never raises on this router tree). The "unmatched" fallback in http_metrics.ex never concatenates with any composed path fragment -- confirmed no leak. Please spot-check this yourself for your own OTP/idiom pass if you'd like independent confirmation; not blocking.

4. FLAGGED DEVIATION -- Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's DB-unavailable handling diverges from design section 6's literal 'the timer poll-and-fire loop for that tick still proceeds normally' wording: when tenant_schemas/0 itself raises, the shipped code skips BOTH the poll-and-fire loop and the active-instances refresh for that tick (calling mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0), rather than attempting the poll-and-fire loop against an undefined/empty list. SECURITY-REVIEWER assessed this as a safe, correctly-reasoned adaptation (the design's literal wording is internally incoherent on this exact failure path -- the loop's own input IS the value that failed to compute) and does NOT require CODE-DESIGNER rework from a safety standpoint. REVIEWER should form its own view on whether this deviation needs a design-doc amendment for future-reader clarity (a documentation/process question) and on whether it is idiomatic OTP failure isolation (it is not a raise-swallowing anti-pattern -- fetch_tenant_schemas/0 rescues once, returns :error, handle_info/2's case handles both branches, schedule_next_tick/0 still runs unconditionally after the case).

SECURITY-REVIEWER's full INV-1..INV-8 disposition, the complete label-allowlist line-by-line audit, the Plug.Router source verification, and the DB-unavailable exposition-leak check are all in handoffs/WF02-REQ194-20260830/security-review-req194.md -- read that file in full before your own gate, per WF-02 Step 2d's own procedure.
